newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian SGB buys most of Tractebel, bids for rest.
newsitem.headline: Belgian SGB buys most of Tractebel, bids for rest.

text.p: Belgian flagship holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Tuesday it had struck a 49 billion franc ($1.6 billion) deal to lift its stake in utility firm Tractebel SA to 65 from 40.5 percent.
It also announced it would launch on October 9 an offer to buy all the remaining shares at the same price of 14,500 francs ($468) each, valuing the total deal at 118 billion francs ($3.8 billion).
Among other interests Tractebel controls Belgian electricity giant Electrabel, gas distributor Distrigas and international energy holding company Powerfin.
SGB, a unit of France's Cie de Suez, said it would pay for the acquisition using a combination of cash and newly-negotiated credit lines.
Holding company Electrafina and insurer Royale Belge, the two firms from which SGB acquired the 25 percent stake in Tractebel on Tuesday, happily announced major profits from the deal.
Royale Belge said it would gross 8.2 billion francs ($300 million) of which four billion francs ($150 million) would be profit. It said it would invest it in its core business of financial services.
Electrafina said the operation would boost its coffers by 41 billion francs ($1.3 billion) -- of which roughly half would be profit. The firm refused comment on what it intended to do with the money.

Electrafina is also the vehicle through which leading Belgian businessman Baron Albert Frere controls Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion SA (CLT), one of the leading players in Europe's television industry.
Frere in the past years has shifted his attention from financial and industrial holdings to the more promising media sector.
Speculation about the deal had been rife for about two weeks, but Tuesday's announcement initially caught the market on the hop.
Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on September 3 that GBL had offered SGB its Tractebel shares at a price of 14,500 francs per share.

Tractebel closed 25 francs higher at 14,100 francs on Tuesday after rising as high as 14,250 francs on the news of the sudden SGB press conference. Before the announcement the share had slipped to 13,950 francs. ($ = 31.10 Belgian Francs)
